taskDescription: Arrange the following steps in the correct sequence for managing a patient presenting with an acute gout attack through to long-term prevention.
paragraphs: Begin anti-inflammatory therapy for the acute attack: NSAID (indomethacin or naproxen), low-dose colchicine, or corticosteroids if the first two are contraindicated.
Continue acute anti-inflammatory treatment for 5–7 days until the attack has fully resolved.
Wait 2–4 weeks after complete resolution of the acute attack before starting any urate-lowering therapy.
Initiate allopurinol at a low dose (100 mg/day) and titrate gradually to achieve a target serum uric acid below 6 mg/dL.
Co-prescribe low-dose colchicine prophylaxis for the first 3–6 months of urate-lowering therapy to prevent mobilisation flares.
Address modifiable risk factors: consider switching thiazide diuretics to losartan, advise dietary purine restriction, and ensure adequate hydration.
